The differential equation that generates the slope field shown above is given by ${y}^{′}=(x-a)(y-b).$ Find the value of $b-a.$
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14045300/assets/a7df5da44a77085b7a89685aa80220a8ae4879cb55c350dba294a5b2e281cac9.png)

 

Notice that the slopes of the slope field are horizontal along the lines $x=-1$ and $y=-2,$ as shown above. Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should evaluate to zero on both of these lines. 

So, our differential equation must be

$$
{y}^{′}=(x+1)(y+2).
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $a=-1,$ $b=-2,$ and $b-a=-1.$
